title: The morphism into projective space over S given by an invertible module and generating sections
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $n\ge0$, and $\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\dots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ the projective space over $S$ of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], a fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of the morphisms $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with structure morphism $q_n=\mathrm{pr}_1:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ and second projection $\mathrm{pr}_2:\mathbf P^n_S\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$. Let $Y$ be a scheme with a morphism $g:Y\to S$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $s_0,\dots,s_n\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ global sections that generate $\mathcal L$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]; equivalently [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre], for every $y\in Y$ some $s_i$ has nonzero image in $\mathcal L_y\otimes\kappa(y)$, which is the form in which [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] states its hypothesis. Let $\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}:Y\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ be the morphism attached to $(\mathcal L,(s_0,\dots,s_n))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] (the unique morphism with $\psi^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$, $\psi^*T_i\mapsto s_i$). The composites $Y\xrightarrow{g}S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $Y\xrightarrow{\psi}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ agree, because $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is terminal [lem-weil-pbc-spec-z-terminal]. Define

$$
\varphi_{g,(\mathcal L,(s_0,\dots,s_n))}:=(g,\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}):Y\longrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S,
$$

the morphism given by the universal property of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]: it is the unique morphism $\varphi$ with $q_n\circ\varphi=\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\varphi=g$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\varphi=\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}$. In particular $\varphi$ is a morphism over $S$ ($Y$ viewed over $S$ by $g$), and a morphism $\chi:Y\to\mathbf P^n_S$ equals $\varphi_{g,(\mathcal L,(s_i))}$ as soon as $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ\chi=g$ and $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\chi=\psi_{(\mathcal L,(s_i))}$ (uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]). It is the morphism 'given on coordinates by $(s_0:\dots:s_n)$'. The index set may be any finite set in place of $\{0,\dots,n\}$ (e.g. $\{0,1\}$ for $\mathbf P^1_S$), and $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_Y$ is allowed.

source.place: Constructions, Section 'Projective space' (label section-projective-space): Lemma (Tag 01NE, label lemma-projective-space), Definition (Tag 01NF, label definition-projective-space) and the paragraph after it: 'Given a scheme Y over S and a pair (L,(s_0,...,s_n)) as in Lemma 01NE the induced morphism to P^n_S is denoted phi_(L,(s_0,...,s_n)) : Y -> P^n_S. This makes sense since the pair defines a morphism into P^n_Z and we already have the structure morphism into S so combined we get a morphism into P^n_S = P^n_Z x S.' (Stacks writes the factors in the order P^n_Z x S; here S is the first factor, as in def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, so q_n = pr_1.) 'generate' is Modules, Definition Tag 01AM.

All kept; the statement now says these explicitly, including uniqueness and that L = O_Y and any finite index set are allowed. Split by one level: every notion has a node. 'Generating sections' had none (the functor-of-points node defines it inline by the fibre condition, Stacks 01NE uses 01AM's surjectivity): created def-weil-pbc-generating-sections (01AM; near match SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections, not a leaf since Epi vs surjective is a theorem) and the claim relating the two forms, lem-weil-pbc-invertible-generating-sections-fibre (01AM + 01CY + Sheaves 0H7H), both unsplit, cited in the statement so that the hypothesis of the functor-of-points lemma is met.
